question: In Newfoundland and Labrador, my child turns five in December of the upcoming school year. Does being four in September automatically make the child ineligible for kindergarten?
generated_answer:
A great question about the nuances of kindergarten eligibility in Newfoundland and Labrador!

According to the Newfoundland and Labrador Department of Education and Early Childhood Development, the eligibility criteria for kindergarten are as follows:

* Children must be five years old by December 31st of the school year in which they are enrolled.

Since your child will turn five in December of the upcoming school year, they would be eligible to start kindergarten in September of that year, even though they will only be four years old at the time.

In other words, being four in September does not automatically make your child ineligible for kindergarten. As long as they will turn five by December 31st of the same year, they can start kindergarten in September.

It's always a good idea to confirm this information with your local school or school district to ensure you have the most up-to-date and accurate information. But based on the provincial guidelines, it seems your child should be eligible to start kindergarten in September, despite being only four years old at the start of the school year.
